# n8n node coverage

Ranked list: `docs/n8n-popular-nodes.txt` (136 node types, most used first).
**Implemented: 105 / 136** (77%). Generated by comparing that list with the node types
registered in `hk-flow` (core, AI), `hk-integrations` (hand-written + `specs/*.json`) and the plugin host.

## How integrations are built
* Core / AI / flow-control nodes: `crates/hk-flow/src/nodes`.
* Hand-written integrations (Slack, Telegram, GitHub, Postgres, Redis, S3, IMAP/SMTP, ...): `crates/hk-integrations/src/*.rs`.
* **Data-driven REST integrations**: one JSON file per service in `crates/hk-integrations/specs/` (resources, operations,
  path, where each parameter goes, pagination). `declarative.rs` expands it into the n8n node description and runs it on the
  shared REST engine; `tests/declarative.rs` checks every operation of every spec against a local server.
* Google and Microsoft services use a **refresh-token credential**: paste client id/secret and a refresh token once; access
  tokens are minted and cached automatically (`oauth.rs`). There is no in-app browser sign-in flow yet.

## Missing (from the ranked list)
aws, awsLambda, awsS3, awsSes, awsSns, box, cron, editImage, facebookGraphApi, ftp, function, functionItem, gmailTrigger, interval, itemLists, kafka, lc:vectorStoreQdrant, linkedIn, microsoftSql, mongoDb, mqtt, mySql, nextCloud, ntfy, oneDrive, rabbitmq, readWriteFile, salesforce, spreadsheetFile, ssh, twitter

Known limits of the declarative nodes: no multipart uploads/downloads (Drive/Dropbox/OneDrive files, WhatsApp media),
Shopify lists return the first 250 rows, Twitter/X and LinkedIn are not included (OAuth user-context flows).
